title: Whole-mount immunofluorescence staining of blood and lymphatic vessels in murine small intestine
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse.
Administer a lethal dose of Ketaminol and Rompun anesthesia via intraperitoneal injection.
Inject in the center of the lower quadra of the abdomen at a 45° angle using a syringe with a 30G needle.
Wait until the mouse is completely anesthetized, i.e., has no responses to tail nor to toe pinches (approximately 3–5 min).
Insert the intake end of the peristaltic pump tubing into a container with ice-cold 2% PFA and flush the tubing and needle with 2% PFA.
Place the mouse on its back and pin its four paws to a Styrofoam board to secure the mouse during perfusion.
Spray 70% ethanol on the fur in the abdominal area.
Grip the chest skin using blunt forceps.
Make an incision along the skin to expose the peritoneum using scissors.
Expose the xiphoid, the piece of arrowhead-shaped white bone, using scissors.
Grip the xiphoid with forceps and make lateral incisions on the peritoneum beneath the ribcage using scissors to expose the diaphragm and the liver.
Cut the diaphragm along the entire length of the ribcage using scissors.
Cut the ribcage on both sides up to the collarbone using scissors.
Lift and pin the freed sternum with the detached ribcage to the Styrofoam board to expose the heart and the lungs.
Carefully remove the pericardial sac or other tissues covering the heart using blunt forceps to provide a clear view of the heart.
Insert the infusion needle attached to the peristaltic pump into the left ventricle at an angle approximately parallel to the midline of the heart.
Insert the infusion needle about 5 mm into the left ventricle to avoid penetration into the left atrium or the right ventricle.
Make a small incision to the right atrium using fine scissors to allow blood to exit from the circulation.
Start perfusion immediately using a peristaltic pump.
Perfuse the mouse with 20 mL of ice-cold 2% PFA over 2 min.
Expose the abdominal organs by cutting the peritoneal wall from the xiphoid down to the symphysis pubis using scissors.
Carefully move the liver lobes aside using blunt forceps to provide a clear view of the stomach.
Grip the stomach with blunt forceps and cut the esophagus and any connective tissues using fine scissors, leaving only the duodenum and the rest of the small intestine attached to the stomach.
Unravel the small intestine from the rest of the gastrointestinal tract by gently pulling the stomach using blunt forceps.
Carefully cut any mesenteric connective and/or fat tissue using fine scissors.
Unravel a minimum of 8 cm of the small intestine starting from the stomach.
Transfer the collected part to a measurement plate.
Place the beginning of the duodenum to the 0 cm mark on the measurement plate.
Isolate the tissue sample by making incisions at marks 3.8 cm and 5.2 cm.
Leave an additional 2 mm to both ends for handling the tissue during preparation.
Grip one end of the tissue sample using blunt forceps.
Fill a syringe with 10 mL of ice-cold 4% PFA.
Attach a plastic gavage needle to the syringe.
Remove any air from the syringe.
Carefully insert the gavage needle into the lumen of the intestinal tube.
Clean the lumen from mucus and possible food remains by flushing with 5 mL of ice-cold 4% PFA while moving the gavage needle back and forth within the lumen.
Grip the other end of the tissue sample using blunt forceps.
Repeat the flushing as previously described.
Place the cleaned tissue sample in ice-cold 4% PFA until dissection.
Transfer the tissue sample to a silicone-coated plate containing ice-cold PBS.
Remove any remains of the mesentery and/or fat attached to the sample using fine forceps and spring scissors.
Cut off the extra 2 mm from both ends of the intestinal tube.
Cut the intestinal tube open longitudinally using spring scissors.
Pin down the tissue sample flat onto a silicone-coated plate with villi facing upwards.
Pin the four corners of the tissue sample onto the silicone-coated plate with insect pins using blunt forceps.
Gently stretch the tissue piece while pinning to ensure it is pinned down flat and straight.
Remove possible dirt and/or mucus from the villi surface using curved forceps.
Add ice-cold 4% PFA to the plate, ensuring enough volume covers the tissue sample without overflow.
Place a lid on the plate and seal with parafilm to prevent liquid leakage.
Fix the sample in 4% PFA at 4°C with rotation for 16–24 hours.
Remove 4% PFA after fixation and wash the sample with PBS at 20°C–25°C with rotation for 4 × 30 minutes.
Remove PBS from the sample.
Wash the sample with 0.3% PBST at 20°C–25°C with rotation for 4 × 30 min.
Remove 0.3% PBST and block the sample in DIM at 20°C–25°C with rotation for 1 h.
Remove DIM and incubate the sample in primary antibodies (goat anti-podocalyxin, 1:400 and rabbit anti-LYVE1, 1:600) diluted in DIM at 4°C with rotation for 2 days.
Wash the sample with 0.3% PBST at 20°C–25°C with rotation for approximately 6 h, changing the solution at least 5 times during this time.

Remove 0.3% PBST and incubate the sample in secondary antibodies (donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor™ Plus 488, 1:1000, and donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor™ Plus 594, 1:1000) diluted in PBS at 4°C for 16–24 h with rotation.
Protect the sample from light during longer incubations by covering the plate with aluminum foil.
Centrifuge secondary antibodies at ≥17,000 g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Use supernatant only from centrifuged secondary antibody mix to avoid speckled staining while imaging.
Remove secondary antibody mix and wash the sample with PBS at 20°C–25°C with rotation for approximately 6 h, changing the solution at least 5 times.
Remove PBS and post-fix the sample with 1% PFA at 20°C–25°C with rotation for 10 min.
Remove PFA and wash the sample with PBS at 20°C–25°C with rotation for 2 × 15 min.
Label a microscope slide with necessary information about the sample (e.g., stainings, experiment information, sample identification number).
Under a dissection microscope, remove any dirt attached to the villi using curved forceps and reposition the pins using blunt forceps if needed.
Cut 1-2 villi thick strips from all four edges of the sample using spring scissors.
Place a small droplet of Mowiol mounting medium on one side of a microscope slide.
Transfer the strips into the mounting medium droplet on the microscope slide using fine forceps.
Position the intestine strips to the center of the microscope slide using fine forceps.
Pull one end of an intestine strip carefully from the mounting medium droplet towards the center of the slide.
Align the pulled strip parallel to the longer edge of the microscope slide.
Ensure that all the villi on a single strip face the same direction.
Grab another intestine strip and position it adjacent to the first strip so that their submucosal sides are in contact.
Ensure that the villi of both strips face outwards from the center of the slide.
Place a cover glass on top of the mounted sample(s).
Fill up the remaining space between the microscope slide and the cover slip with Mowiol mounting medium using a 200 μL pipette.
Avoid air bubbles during application of the mounting medium.
Seal all four edges of the cover glass with nail polish.
Let the seal dry completely before proceeding.
Store the mounted sample horizontally on a flat surface at 4°C and protect it from light until imaging.
Image the samples using a ZEISS LSM 780 confocal microscope.
